old_title: Ukraine war live: Putin told he 'must stop' Russian strike destroys WHO warehouse
new_title: Ukraine war live: Zelensky mocks Putin's reliance on North Korea after deadly strike
old_text:
A WHO warehouse full of medical equipment and other humanitarian supplies has been struck and destroyed in a Russian strike on Ukraine.
The WHO's director-general said UN workers tried to evacuate health supplies from the Dnipro facility but some 170 pallets - more than half - were still inside when it was hit.
"I cannot say loudly enough: attacks on health care MUST STOP," Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus posted on X.
"Otherwise, people are deprived of lifesaving healthcare. Even wars have rules. One of those is that health must be protected!"
It comes as Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky claimed North Korea was preparing to deploy as many as 50,000 soldiers to support Russia's war effort.
Zelensky said North Korea would benefit from "experience in modern warfare" as well as receiving licences to produce more advanced Russian technology.
He appealed to South Korea to respond by providing support "in an area where we have a shortage", referring to its air defence systems.
Earlier, UK defence secretary Wes Streeting urged allies to strengthen Ukraine's air defences ahead of winter, warning that Vladimir Putin will seek to use the colder months as a "weapon" against Kyiv.
Russia says air defences intercepted 285 Ukrainian drones over 12-hour period
Russia's defence ministry said on Sunday that its air defence units had intercepted and destroyed 285 Ukrainian drones over a 12-hour period.
The ministry said the drones were downed between 8am and 8pm Moscow time (0500-1700 GMT), with most incidents reported over central and western Russian regions. The attacks also included Bashkortostan, a region between the Volga River and the Ural Mountains.
Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on Telegram that air defence units had destroyed five drones heading towards the capital, where such attacks have become a regular occurrence during the more than four-year war between Russia and Ukraine.
Pictures show street market in Kyiv
Street markets continue to operate in Ukraine despite the destruction and disruption caused by Russia's war.
The market was damaged in the latest attacks as Russia continues its strikes across Ukraine.
Several killed after Ukrainian drone strike in Russia's Tatarstan, mayor claims
Ukrainian drones have carried out a deadly drone attack on industrial and civilian targets in the city of Nizhnekamsk in Russia's Tatarstan region which killed a number of people, Radmir Belyayev, the city's mayor said in a statement on Telegram.
Nizhnekamsk hosts a major oil refinery.
According to monitoring channels, Ukrainian forces launched strikes on a Russian oil refinery in Tatarstan overnight on Monday.
Eyewitnesses posted footage showing drones flying over the Russian city of Nizhnekamsk.
Ukraine accuses Unicef of failing to hold Russia accountable for children's deaths
The Ukrainian foreign minister has criticised Unicef for failing to condemn Russia over the deaths of children in Ukraine.
In the statement last week at the UN, Unicef called for Russia and Ukraine to follow obligations under international humanitarian law, but did not mention that Russia was behind deadly strikes that killed Ukrainian children in recent days.
It also did not recognise Russia's responsibility for starting its war against Ukraine.
"It is deeply deplorable that Unicef missed the essential point in its statement: All these children's deaths are a direct result of Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine. By presenting these casualties without this essential context, Unicef creates a false equivalence between the aggressor and the victim," Andrii Sybiha said in a post to X.
"Moreover, Unicef's statement lacks basic fact-checking. It failed to mention that the casualties in Russia's Krasnodar were caused by a drone reportedly intercepted by Russian air defence. It also failed to verify the information on casualties in Ukraine: seven, not three, children from one family were killed in the Dnipropetrovsk Oblast", Sybiha said.
Six die in Ukrainian drone attack on Belgorod, Russian authorities say
Six people died in a Ukrainian overnight drone attack on the Russian city of Belgorod, the regional crisis centre said on Sunday.
Alexander Shuvayev, the acting governor of Belgorod region, earlier said three people were killed and 25 others, including two children, were injured.
The death toll later rose to six after officials said emergency crews combed an apartment building which had been set ablaze.
Shuvayev said the attack sparked fires in two apartment buildings and a large number of residential and non-residential buildings were damaged.
Russia's defence ministry said it had destroyed more than 150 Ukrainian drones over the European part of the country, as well as over Crimea, the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.
In Novorossiysk, a major Russian export port on the Black Sea, drone debris fell on two facilities, local mayor Andrei Kravchenko said, without identifying the sites.
The local crisis centre later said three residential buildings were damaged and one person was injured.
In Bashkortostan region, a Ukrainian drone struck a building under construction and a crane in the city of Ufa, state-run RIA news agency reported, citing local emergency services
WHO warehouse destroyed in Dnipro, Tedros says
A WHO humanitarian warehouse in Dnipro, Ukraine, was struck and destroyed last Friday, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said.No casualties were reported.
A WHO staff member and drivers had left the site earlier in the day after helping evacuate 130 of around 300 pallets of medical supplies intended for frontline health facilities.
"I cannot say loudly enough: attacks on health care must stop. Otherwise, people are deprived of lifesaving healthcare," Mr Adhanom Ghebreyesus posted.
"Even wars have rules. One of those is that health must be protected!"
Russia says it captures two villages in eastern Ukraine
Russian forces have taken control of two villages in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region, the state-run RIA news agency reported on Sunday, citing the Russian defence ministry.
The ministry report on Telegram said Russian forces had seized Vasyutinske, a few kilometres east of the "fortress city" of Kramatorsk, and Toretsk, southwest of the city of Druzhkivka.
Ukrainian forces made no acknowledgement of the two settlements changing hands.
Russia is slowly advancing westward through Donetsk region, though there has been little significant change for months in the positions along the 1,200km (775mile) frontline.
The Ukrainian war blog DeepState, which uses open source reports in documenting the frontline positions of both sides, reported that Russian forces had made advances near Illinivka -- outside the contested city of Kostiantynivka.
It also reported Russian advances near Chasiv Yar, to the west of the city of Bakhmut, which fell to Russian forces in 2023 after long months of heavy fighting.
The Ukrainian military's General Staff, in a late evening report, said Kyiv's forces had repelled 24 attacks around Kostiantynivka, Illinivka and other centres.
Russian commanders said last month their forces had seized Kostiantynivka, but Ukrainian officials have disputed the claim.
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky in his nightly video address on Sunday made no reference to changes in frontline positions, but singled out for praise Ukrainian forces fighting in specific areas, notably Dobropillia, Kostiantynivka and Kramatorsk.
War entering a 'new phase', military analyst says
Military analyst Michael Clarke has said that the war is entering a "new phase".
While Russia is making "incremental progress" and Ukraine is "hitting back locally", he described the advances as "snail's pace stuff".
Speaking to Sky News, he said that the two countries are "hurting each other now to a degree that is going to push it to some sort of crisis".
"Russia has a much greater capacity to be hurt because it hasn't been hurt very much so far as a society."
He said that Kyiv is "poking the bear in the eye" by escalating attacks and said that it is a "dangerous assumption" to expect Moscow to back down.
Clarke said that Putin's "next best option" may be to "frighten" Ukraine's European allies into reducing their support for Kyiv.
'Frightened and disorientated' cat found in ruins of Kharkiv flats
Emergency workers responding to a Russian attack on a Kharkiv tower block found a frightened cat from the rubble.
Rescue workers were digging through the remains of the building to rescue residents when they found a cat inside the rubble and rescued it.
Ukraine's state emergency service said "Barney" was found "frightened and disorientated, alone amidst the ruins".
The male cat was carefully rescued and his owner was on her way to pick up her cat, the spokesperson said.
"Behind the rubble - someone's life, and we cherish each one."
Two people were killed and 16 were injured in the strike in Ukraine's second-largest city, authorities said on Sunday.
Ukraine's Zelensky says up to 50,000 North Korean troops to be deployed in Russia
Volodymyr Zelensky has said up to 50,000 North Korean soldiers will be deployed in Russia to fight for Pyongyang's ally, while calling on South Korea to provide support for its air defence.
Zelensky said on X on Saturday that "a decision has been made for 30,000 to 50,000 North Koreans to be deployed on the territory of Russia", a higher figure than his estimate of 30,000 in July.
He did not elaborate on how he obtained the information. He said Kyiv had found some North Korean missiles in Ukraine's territory, without disclosing their locations.
"It is absolutely clear that North Korea will continue to build its experience in modern warfare, receive licences from Russia, and receive all kinds of military tools from them," he said.
Urging Seoul to have closer cooperation with Kyiv, Zelensky said that Ukraine "would very much like to receive support from South Korea in an area where we have a shortage", referring to its air defence systems.
"We are ready to work on the Drone Deal and other areas as well," he said, adding that Ukrainian diplomats "are in contact" with Seoul to push potential deals.
North Korea has so far sent an estimated 14,000 soldiers to Russia's Kursk Region in 2024, helping Moscow beat back a major incursion into the region by Ukrainian forces.
new_text:
Volodymyr Zelensky has mocked Vladimir Putin for his reliance on ally North Korea, saying Russia is no longer capable of waging its war on Ukraine alone.
In his nightly video address, Zelensky said Russia was preparing to deploy an additional North Korean contingent on its territory and has also received additional ballistic missiles from North Korea.
"For the first time in its history, Russia cannot wage war without reinforcements from North Korea," he said.
He also issued a warning to countries in Asia, saying North Korea will present a "greater danger" to Japan, South Korea and the Philippines as it gains military experience, correcting any shortcomings in the process.
On Monday, a Ukrainian drone attack hit targets over 600 miles deep inside Russia. The strikes hit both industrial and civilian infrastructure in the city of Nizhnekamsk and the Taneco oil refinery in the Tatarstan region.
At least 13 people, including seven Uzbek citizens and one child, were killed in the attacks.
A period of mourning has been declared in the region, according to the mayor of Nizhnekamsk, Radmir Belayev, in a post on Telegram.
Seven Uzbek citizens killed in drone attack on Russia's Tatarstan region, consulate says
Seven Uzbek citizens were killed in a drone attack in Russia's Tatarstan region on Monday, the Uzbek consulate in Kazan said.
The consulate did not immediately provide further details about the victims.
They were among 13 people, including a child, killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on industrial and civilian targets in the city of Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan region, some 680 miles from the border with Ukraine.
It was one of Ukraine's deadliest and deepest strikes inside Russia.
Between two and three million citizens of Uzbekistan, Central Asia's most populous country, work in Russia, with the Uzbek economy partly based on remittances from migrants.
Uzbekistan has struck a diplomatic balance on the war in Ukraine, maintaining close ties with Russia while also stressing support for Ukraine's territorial integrity.
Drone attack kills one in Russia's Voronezh region
A drone attack killed one person and injured two others in Russia's Voronezh region overnight, while falling debris triggered fires at warehouse facilities, Alexander Gusev, the regional governor, said on Tuesday.
Russia's air defence units destroyed 15 drones over the city of Voronezh and five districts of the region, Gusev said on Telegram.
"A drone crash caused fires at two warehouses of a large company. At one facility, the fire has been contained to an area of 16,000 square meters, while at the other, a blaze covering 20,000 square meters is being extinguished. Emergency services are on scene," the governor said.
He did not identify the company whose warehouses were affected.
Earlier on Tuesday, Russian online retailer Wildberries said its logistics facilities in the Voronezh region had been evacuated in accordance with safety requirements.
Pictures show massive fire and damaged buildings in Zaporizhzhia
Five people were killed and 20 were injured after a Russian attack in the southeastern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia early on Tuesday.
Zaporizhzhia regional governor Ivan Fedorov said Russian troops deployed missiles and aerial bombs on the city.
Pictures showed buildings and vehicles ablaze. Air raid alerts were sounded in both Zaporizhzhia and in Kyiv.
Zelensky says Russia cannot wage war without North Korea's help
Volodymyr Zelensky has mocked Vladimir Putin for his reliance on ally North Korea, saying that: "For the first time in its history, Russia cannot wage war without reinforcements from North Korea."
He said Russia was preparing to deploy an additional North Korean contingent on its territory and has also received additional ballistic missiles from North Korea.
"Everyone around the world must understand what this means. This is not only about the lives of people in Ukraine, and not only about the threats we face," he said in his nightly address.
"North Korea's ballistic missiles and other weapons are being improved through its collaboration with Russia."
He also issued a warning to countries in Asia, saying North Korea will present a "greater danger" to Japan, South Korea and Philippines as it gains military experience, correcting any shortcomings in the process.
"That is why, when we speak about the need for joint action, for coordination and mutual support, when we speak about the need to help us strengthen our air defence, we are also, in fact, speaking about taking away North Korea's appetite and any interest in coming here - to our land and into our skies - with its weapons in order to learn how to wage war," he said.
Ukrainian MiG-29 aircraft lost after catching fire
A Ukrainian MiG-29 fighter jet caught fire and was lost during a combat mission, with the pilot ejecting safely, the Ukrainian Air Force said on Monday.
A statement on the Telegram messaging app said the pilot was targeting Russian positions while in the southern region of Odesa.
"According to preliminary data, during the launch of a missile, an emergency situation occurred, causing the plane to catch fire and the pilot to lose control, even though he tried to save the aircraft," the statement said.
The Air Force said the pilot ejected safely and was transported to a hospital. The cause of the crash was under investigation.
Russian attack on Kyiv triggers fires, officials say
Russian forces attacked the Ukrainian capital Kyiv with missiles early on Tuesday, triggering fires in the city centre, officials said.
The city's military administration said warehouses in a central district were ablaze. One person was reported injured.
The air raid alert was in effect for about 40 minutes before officials declared the all clear.
Mayor Vitali Klitschko said medical personnel had been dispatched to a central district.
Russian forces also deployed missiles and bombs in an attack on the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia, regional Governor Ivan Fedorov said on Telegram.
Swedish security service says it broke up Russian spy plot
Sweden's security service says it shut down a Russian spying operation that had tried to influence decision-making there and discredit the Nordic country and its EU and NATO allies.
The operation had been planned and directed by Russia's SVR foreign intelligence service and involved three people working under the cover of diplomatic immunity, Sweden's SAPO service said on Monday.
"This is consistent with the threat we see Russia posing," a SAPO spokesperson told Reuters.
They said the individuals allegedly involved "are no longer in Sweden" and that they have "been able to break up this operation".
The spokesperson declined to give any further information about the operation or the actions taken by the security service.
Russia blocks last anti-war party from upcoming parliamentary election
Russia has effectively shut down a key avenue for voting against the war in the upcoming elections, as most of Vladimir Putin's opponents remain jailed or in exile.
The supreme court upheld a case brought by the small pro-Kremlin nationalist party Rodina to strip voters opposed to the war of their last chance to vote for Yabloko, the country's last remaining anti-war party.
The court barred Yabloko's entire slate of federal election candidates from running for seats in Russia's State Duma.
Following the ruling, hundreds of Yabloko supporters gathered outside the courthouse to protest, as security forces prepared to disperse the crowd. Protesters chanted "Shame! Shame!" as about 500 people gathered outside the court.
Addressing the protesters, Yabloko leader Nikolay Rybakov said the party would appeal the decision.
Yabloko is the only liberal party still operating in Russia, while most of Putin's opponents are jailed, exiled or dead.
Alternative voting options to Putin's de facto party, the ruling United Russia, are tolerated only when they are too weak to win, support the Kremlin or act as "spoilers" by drawing votes away from candidates who could pose a threat to the regime.
The party told AFP over the weekend that 40 of its activists were facing prosecution for opposing the war.
Its deputy leader, Maxim Kruglov, was jailed for seven months in June over social media posts, while Rybakov was fined and barred from elections after posting a picture with Alexei Navalny.
Ukraine and Saudi Arabia discuss defence and food security
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky said he discussed a drone deal and food security with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Monday.
"There are domains in which Ukraine and Saudi Arabia can strengthen each other's ability to protect lives and people," he said on X after the call.
Speaking later in his nightly video address, Zelensky said a team of Ukrainian officials was in the region "and there are already areas in which our relations are developing well. I am counting on reciprocity in our mutual support.
"Ukraine and Saudi Arabia signed an agreement on military cooperation in March when the president met the crown prince.
Ukraine has developed expertise in dealing with Iranian-designed drones over more than 4-1/2 years of war with Russia.
It has also signed deals on drone development with other countries in the Middle East and Gulf and elsewhere.
He said they also discussed Saudi Arabia's recent defence agreements with Türkiye and Pakistan.
Russia to hand over control of two key Mediterranean bases to Syria
Russian forces will relinquish control of two strategically vital Mediterranean coastal bases, Syria's foreign ministry says, and they will be transformed into joint training centres under a new bilateral agreement.
The development signals a significant recalibration of Moscow's military footprint in the region.
The Hmeimem air base and the Tartus naval base served as crucial Russian military outposts in the eastern Mediterranean throughout Syria's civil war.
Russia was the primary political and military ally of former president Bashar al-Assad, who was ousted in December 2024 by Isis-affiliated insurgents led by now-leader Ahmad al-Sharaa, known by the nom de guerre Abu Mohammed al-Jolani, and subsequently sought exile in Russia.

Russia Volodymyr Zelensky has said up to 50,000 North Korean soldiers will be deployed in Russia to fight for Pyongyang's ally, while calling on South Korea to provide support for its air defence. Zelensky said on X on Saturday that "a decision has been made for 30,000 to 50,000 North Koreans to be deployed on the territory of Russia", a higher figure than his estimate of 30,000 in July. He did not elaborate on how he obtained the information. He said Kyiv had found some North Korean missiles in Ukraine's territory, without disclosing their locations. "It is absolutely clear that North Korea will continue to build its experience in modern warfare, receive licences from Russia, and receive all kinds of military tools from them," he said. Urging Seoul to have closer cooperation with Kyiv, Zelensky said that Ukraine "would very much like to receive support from South Korea in an area where we have a shortage", referring to its air defence systems. "We are ready to work on the Drone Deal and other areas as well," he said, adding that Ukrainian diplomats "are in contact" with Seoul to push potential deals. North Korea has so far sent an estimated 14,000 soldiers to Russia's Kursk Region in 2024, helping Moscow beat back a major incursion into the region by Ukrainian forces.
